## Install and load

```{r}
remotes::install_github("vigliafg/rstats-commander",
                        subdir = "plugins/RcmdrShinyPlugin.FactoMineR")
RcmdrShiny::run(plugins = "RcmdrShinyPlugin.FactoMineR")
```

## Principal component analysis

```{r}
.pca <- FactoMineR::PCA(decathlon[, c("100m", "Long.jump", "Shot.put",
                                       "High.jump", "400m")], graph = TRUE)
summary(.pca)
```

Supplementary quantitative or categorical variables can be added in the dialog;
they appear in the output but do not drive the components.

## Correspondence analysis

**FactoMineR > Correspondence analysis...** works on a contingency table:

```{r}
.ca <- FactoMineR::CA(table(dataset$row, dataset$column), graph = TRUE)
```

## Multiple correspondence analysis

For a set of factors:

```{r}
.mca <- FactoMineR::MCA(dataset[, c("f1", "f2", "f3")], graph = TRUE)
```

## Multiple factor analysis

MFA and DMFA group the variables; enter the group sizes in the dialog, in the
same order as the selected variables.

```{r}
.mfa <- FactoMineR::MFA(dataset[, variables], group = c(3, 2, 4),
                        graph = TRUE)
```

## Clustering

HCPC takes an existing FactoMineR result:

```{r}
.hcpc <- FactoMineR::HCPC(.pca)
summary(.hcpc)
```

The dialog expects the name of the object in the R session, for example `.pca`.

## Category description

```{r}
FactoMineR::catdes(dataset, num.var = dataset$group)
```

## Reading the output

- The **eigenvalues** table gives the share of variance per dimension.
- **Variable coordinates** show which variables contribute to each axis.
- **Individuals** with large cos2 drive the shape of the cloud.
- Plots are captured in the **Plots** tab.

## Limits

HCPC operates on an existing result object rather than fitting the analysis from
scratch, and the graphical options exposed in the dialog are a subset of
FactoMineR's.
